column1: # Per-file TIMEOUT ALLOWANCE registry for tools/run-perl-suite.pl.
# The effective per-file timeout is max(seconds, --timeout).  Registering a
# file here is NOT an excuse and NOT a skip: the file still runs, still
# reports, still fails the run if it diverges.  What it buys is that the file
# gets measured AT ALL — a file that TIMEOUTs contributes NO TAP rows, so its
# passing rows vanish from the signal without anything saying so (the #176
# pack.t lesson: a file invisible to the gate reads as "0 new failures").
#  - one line per file, with a CAUSE naming why it needs the time (and the
#    measurement it was sized from) — an allowance without a cause is a
#  - size it from a measured run, then round up ~1.5x for machine load;
#  - when a file gets faster, DELETE its row (the allowance is a max, so a
#    stale row costs nothing on a fast run, but it misreports the file).
